In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the STM data are consistent with the topological network model, but that the data do not exclude a conventional d-wave model.
the k-space octet of subgap resonances and chequerboard r-space pattern are both consistent with the ferroelastic nanodomains model.

the subgap resonances in the STM images of BSCCO are a consequence of a topologically stable octet of k-space quasiparticle states that are consistent in energy, wavevector and spatial extent with the quasiparticles observed by ARPES, but the origin of this octet of k-states is the consequence of the filamentary ferroelectric nanodomain model of BSCCO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the STM k-space octets are a topological consequence of the ferroelastic nanodomains, and the octets are a consequence of the nanodomains rather than a consequence of a d-wave superconducting gap.
the STM subgap resonances are a consequence of the network topology of the CuO2 ferroelastic nanodomains and the associated electron–phonon interaction.
the high-temperature superconductor (HTS) cuprates have a network of nanoscale ferroelastic domains that form the subgap chequerboard observed by STM and ARPES.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high-temperature superconductor cuprates are not d-wave superconductors, and that the d-wave symmetry is an artefact of the surface d-wave gap.
the high-intensity octets are a consequence of the network topology of a ferroelastic nanodomains and are unrelated to the d-wave gap or any other superconducting properties.
the high-temperature superconductor cuprates exhibit anisotropic surface states with d-wave symmetry that are consistent with ARPES, but are not the result of a conventional d-wave superconductor.
